[[TASK-DEFINITION]] You will be given a worked example. Your job is to translate the [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] according to the [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]]. [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] [[PROGRAM-NAME]] Rotating the List Values to the Left by Two Position [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]] Construct a program that has a function that receives a list of values and returns the list rotated to the left by 2 position so that the value at the front of the list goes to the second last position, the second value of the list goes to the back, and the order of the other values stays the same. For example, if the list is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], the program will change it to [3, 4, 5, 6, 1, 2]. [[SOURCE-CODE]] [[LINE01]] #Step 1: Define the function [[LINE02]] def rotate_left_by_2(lst): [[LINE03]] #Step 1.1: Store the first two values of the list in local variables [[LINE04]] first = lst[0] [[LINE05]] second = lst[1] [[LINE06]] #Step 1.2: Rotate the remaining values of the list to the left by 2 position [[LINE07]] for i in range(len(lst)-2): [[LINE08]] lst[i] = lst[i + 2] [[LINE09]] #Step 1.3: Move the first two values of the list to the back of the list [[LINE10]] lst[len(lst)-2] = first [[LINE11]] lst[len(lst)-1] = second [[LINE12]] return lst [[LINE13]] #Step 2: Call the function [[LINE14]] values = [3, 8, 9, 8, 7, 5] [[LINE15]] print("Original list:", values) [[LINE16]] print("Rotated list: ", rotate_left_by_2(values)) [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]] [[LINE02.EXPL1]] We need to first declare the function so that we can call it later. The following lines declare the function rotate_left_by_2 that takes a list, rotates the list to the left by 2 position, and returns the rotated list.

Note that all statements following the header line are indented. [[LINE04.EXPL1]] The first two values are supposed to go to back of the list, and the other values are supposed to rotate forward. We can make the task easier by storing the two values at the front of the list into local variables and then shift the other values to the left by two position.

This statement stores the element at index 0 (i.e., value at the front of the list) in the variable first. We will use variable first later to move the value at the front to the second last position of the list. [[LINE05.EXPL1]] The first two values are supposed to go to back of the list, and the other values are supposed to rotate forward. We can make the task easier by storing the two values at the front of the list into local variables and then shift the other values to the left by two position.

This statement stores the element at index 1 (i.e., second value of the list) in the variable second. We will use variable second later to move the second value of the list to the back of the list. [[LINE07.EXPL1]] With first and second value safely tucked away, we now have to shift the remaining values to the left by 2 position. We could break down the overall task into shifting operations, each of which is a simple assignment statement. Because of repeated shift operations on the list values, we’d want to write this with a for loop. We’ll replace the element at index i with the value currently stored at index i+2, this will shift the value at index i+2 to the left, by two position. [[LINE07.EXPL2]] Note that, instead of range(len(lst)), we need to use range(len(lst)-2)). The reason is that in the assignment statement in the loop body we always move the value two position ahead of the value at the current index. So, to shift all the remaining values, we need to iterate through indexes that start at 0 with every integer number up to but not including len(lst)-2. [[LINE07.EXPL3]] Note that len(lst) returns the number of the values in the list. Also, note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header. [[LINE08.EXPL1]] We need to shift value at index i+2 to value at index i. We do this by setting the value at index i to the value at index i+2. [[LINE10.EXPL1]] After shifting the values to the left, we’ve made room at the end of the list for the first value that used to be at the front of the list (which is currently stored in local variable called first). This statement copies the value of variable first to the index of the second last element in the list. [[LINE10.EXPL2]] Note that len(lst)-2 is the index of the second last element in the list. [[LINE11.EXPL1]] After shifting the values to the left, we’ve made room at the end of the list for the second value that used to be at the front of the list (which is currently stored in local variable called second). This statement copies the value of variable second to the index of the last element in the list. [[LINE11.EXPL2]] Note that len(lst)-1 is the index of the last element in the list. [[LINE12.EXPL1]] Now that we finished rotating the list values, we need to return the rotated list. The return statement, when reached, ends the function call and sends the result back to the caller. [[LINE14.EXPL1]] We define the list referred by variable values to hold specified numbers. We initialize the list by separating values with a comma and enclosing the collection in square brackets [ ]. [[LINE15.EXPL1]] This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Original list:" followed by the content of the list.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end. [[LINE15.EXPL2]] Note that we can see the content of the list by calling the print function and passing the list to that. [[LINE16.EXPL1]] This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Rotated list: " followed by the content of the list returned from the function call.

Note that any changes that were made to the list within the rotate_left_by_2 function affect the original list in the calling function. That is, after the function call, the list referred by variables values will be changed to the rotated list. [[LINE16.EXPL2]] Note that we do not necessarily have to store the returned list from the function call in a variable. We could use the list returned from the function call directly in the print function. [[LINE16.EXPL3]] The function call must be done after the function is declared. Also note that we can see the content of the list by calling the print function and passing the list to that.
